goal: A reusable, self-hosted (static HTML/CSS/JS, no build step) slide-deck template for Zone01 Athens study guides. One shared engine (static/) is reused across many lesson topics; only the small index.html per lesson changes. Content (theory + gamified checkpoints) is meant to be generated/edited by an LLM in Greek prose with English code comments, so the engine's HTML surface (class names, opts, exact JS call syntax) must stay well-documented and self-explanatory to an LLM working from index.html's top instructions comment alone.

file_architecture.index.html: Per-lesson file. Top of file has a large HTML comment documenting the whole API (addContent/addQuiz/addFillBlank/addMatching, opts, background options, spoiler markup, html tag whitelist) so an LLM can regenerate/extend content correctly without seeing any other file. Body contains: #progress-track/#progress-fill, #slide-bg-layer (sibling of #deck, see below), #deck (empty, JS-populated), #nav-bar (Reset Progress / Return link to https://avgerinos8.github.io/Zone01Guides / Back / dots / counter / Next), <link> to static/style.css THEN static/theme-<name>.css, <script> to static/script.js and static/highlighter.js, then one inline <script> at the bottom with the actual course content calls ending in initSlideDeck({version:"X.Y.Z"}).
file_architecture.static/style.css: Shared theme/layout engine, same file reused by every lesson. :root holds --tone-1..5 (+ -rgb pairs), --tone-text(+rgb), --code-bg(+rgb) as FALLBACK DEFAULTS (currently burgundy palette) — real theming happens via a second stylesheet loaded after this one (see theme files). Semantic aliases (--bg,--panel,--ink,--accent,--danger + rgb) all resolve through --tone-*. --correct/--wrong are fixed green/red, deliberately outside the 5-tone palette. --syn-* are VS-Code-Dark+-style code-token colors, independent of the page theme. Contains all component styling: slides/transitions, quiz, fill-in-the-blank, matching pairs, glossary (3 layout variants), spoiler, nav bar, mobile breakpoints (900px, 720px, 480px).
file_architecture.static/theme-burgundy.css / static/theme: Tiny (~25 line) files containing ONLY :root { --tone-1..5(+rgb), --tone-text(+rgb), --code-bg(+rgb) } — nothing else. Loaded via a SECOND <link> in index.html, after style.css, so the cascade overrides style.css's fallback values. This replaced an earlier design where each lesson had its OWN full duplicated copy of the entire stylesheet just to change 14 color lines — now every lesson shares one style.css and picks a theme file.
file_architecture.static/script.js: Shared rendering/navigation engine, same file reused by every lesson. Exposes addContent/addQuiz/addFillBlank/addMatching (push onto a module-level `slides` array), shuffleSeed (deterministic per-question option shuffling), decorateCodeBlocks (auto copy-button on every <pre>), decorateSpoilers (wires up drag-to-reveal), renderQuestion/renderFillBlank/renderMatching/buildInteractiveHeader (per-type UI builders), a scoring subsystem (savedScores, scoreTier, createScoreBadge/refreshScoreBadge, computeTotalScore/updateTotalScoreDisplay), a persistence subsystem (per-page localStorage key prefix derived from URL path, checkCourseVersion for auto-reset-on-version-bump, persistAnswers/persistScores/persistCurrentSlide, performHardReset), updateBackgroundLayer (syncs the single shared #slide-bg-layer to the active slide's opts, called from goTo()), renderSlide(el, contentEl, slide, idx) and initSlideDeck(config) which builds the DOM and wires navigation/keyboard/swipe.
file_architecture.static/highlighter.js: Standalone, independent, IIFE-wrapped auto syntax highlighter. Put class="lang-go|lang-js|lang-html|lang-css|lang-bash|lang-docker|lang-yml|lang-json|lang-generic" on any element and it colors it automatically (via the same --syn-*/tok-* tokens used elsewhere) — a MutationObserver catches slides added dynamically by script.js. lang-generic only grays out line comments (#, //, --) for languages without a dedicated highlighter. lang-bash also colors segments distinctly (author must write them as <placeholder> in source HTML, or the browser eats them as unknown tags before the highlighter ever runs). This is SEPARATE from the manual word hand-coloring approach documented in index.html's comment — either approach works, highlighter.js is just less typing when its language list covers what's needed.
file_architecture.lessons/*.html (e.g. 07-Docker.html, 08-: Real, in-use lesson files — same structure as index.html's template but with actual content. Each links the SAME shared static/style.css + its own static/theme-*.css.

js_api_reference.addContent(html, opts?): One content slide (theory, title, glossary, sources, etc.) from a raw HTML string.
js_api_reference.addQuiz(question | [question,...], opts?: One or more MC questions on one slide. question = { q, options:[4 strings], correct:index, explain }.
js_api_reference.addFillBlank(item | [item,...], opts?): One or more fill-in-the-blank code exercises. item = { code (blanks marked __id__), blanks:[{id,answer}], explain }. UI is fully automatic: Check button grades it; Reveal-hint button (placed ABOVE the hints list so it never shifts position) reveals one still-empty answer per click without saying which slot, and is replaced by a disabled '[Time to Guess]' label when the item has only 1 blank; a wrong answer after Check shows a diagonal red strike (~2px, CSS var --fb-strike-width) across the input plus the correct value floating above-right in green (outlined in --code-bg for legibility over any background), positioned above the strike line (z-index).
js_api_reference.addMatching(pairs | [set1, set2, ...], o: pairs = [{term,def},...] for one matching game. Pass an array of pair-arrays to stack 2-3 independent sets on one slide, each with its own score/reset and an automatic 'Set N / M' label when there's more than one. On screens <=900px the two columns stay SIDE BY SIDE (never stack vertically) by shrinking gap/font-size/padding progressively (extra tier at <=480px).

opts_object.label: string, overrides default header text (quiz/fillblank/matching)
opts_object.note: Greek string, short instructional note under the header (quiz/fillblank/matching)
opts_object.bg: background image path; works on ALL 4 add* functions
opts_object.overlayAlpha: 0..1, default 0.5 - solid overlay over the bg image for text readability
opts_object.backgroundSize: real CSS value: cover | contain | auto(default) | "100% 100%"(stretch) | "100% auto"(fit-width)
opts_object.backgroundRepeat: real CSS value: no-repeat(default) | repeat | repeat-x | repeat-y
opts_object.backgroundPosition: real CSS value, default "top left", e.g. "center center"

background_image_architecture: A SINGLE shared #slide-bg-layer div, a sibling of #deck (NOT nested inside any .slide), position:fixed, updated by updateBackgroundLayer() in script.js's goTo() whenever the active slide changes. This was a deliberate redesign after two earlier approaches failed: (1) position:fixed pseudo-elements per .slide broke the vertical scrollbar because .slide.active also had a transform-based swipe animation, and CSS makes a transformed element the containing block for its own fixed descendants, corrupting scroll-area calculation during the transition; (2) switching those pseudo-elements to position:absolute fixed THAT bug but reintroduced the original problem - absolutely-positioned descendants of a scrolling container scroll away WITH its content, they are not visually pinned (only position:fixed or position:sticky achieve that). The final fix also required splitting .slide (scrolls, never transforms, hosts nothing) from a new .slide-content wrapper (never scrolls itself, plays the swipe transform) so the swipe animation and the scrolling container are no longer the same element.
other_known_css_gotcha: `.slide` must set BOTH overflow-y and overflow-x explicitly. Per the CSS Overflow spec, if only one axis is set to something other than 'visible', the browser silently computes the other axis as 'auto' too - this caused unwanted horizontal scroll/pan (draggable via middle-click) even with nothing visibly overflowing, until overflow-x:hidden was added explicitly.
spoiler_minigame:
Drag-to-reveal block, embeddable inside any addContent() HTML:
Drag to reveal ->' style text
...
. Diagonal-striped 'locked' look (repeating-linear-gradient 45deg). Unlocks ONLY on an actual drag past ~40% of its width (click/tap alone does nothing) - wired automatically by decorateSpoilers() in script.js, supports mouse (Pointer Events) and touch. Known limitation: reveal state is NOT persisted to localStorage yet - resets on page reload.
scoring_system: Every quiz question / fillblank item / matching set gets an automatic score: 100 = fully correct, 0 = wrong, 50 = fillblank answered with at least one hint revealed (regardless of eventual correctness), matching set = % of its pairs currently matched. A small 'Score: N%' badge (color-tiered: >=70 green / 40-69 accent / <40 red) sits next to each slide's own 'Reset this quiz' button, refreshed live on every interaction. The deck-wide aggregate is written into whichever element has id="final-score" (must be placed once, typically on the sources/last slide) - three text states: not started yet, 'Αποτέλεσμα SO FAR: N%' while incomplete, 'Αποτέλεσμα: N%' once every scorable item has been answered. Unanswered items count as 0 toward the total (not excluded from the average).
persistence: localStorage, keyed by a prefix derived from the page's URL path (so multiple lesson files never collide). Stores current slide index, all answers (including fill-blank input values + revealed-hint ids + checked state, and matched-pair ids), and all scores. A course `version` string (passed to initSlideDeck) auto-wipes stored progress for that page when bumped - use this whenever a content/scoring-format change would make old stored data stale or misleading.
syntax_highlighting_for_addContent_code: Two independent options: (1) hand-wrap tokens yourself with <span class="tok-kw|tok-type|tok-str|tok-com|tok-num|tok-func">, guaranteed to work with zero setup; (2) put class="lang-go|js|html|css|bash|docker|yml|json|generic" on the <code> element and static/highlighter.js colors it automatically at runtime via the same token classes. Either way, escape < > & as < > & in the raw code text (it sits inside HTML) - literal unescaped angle brackets (e.g. a bash placeholder like <container-name>) get silently swallowed by the browser as unknown HTML tags before either highlighting method ever sees them.
html_tags_for_addContent: h1 h2 h3 p p.lede div.callout(span.tag+text) div.callout.good div.grid2>div.card(h3+p) div.grid3>div.card(h3+p) pre>code table.glossary-table>tr>td.gt-term+td.gt-def div.glossary-strip>div.gs-pill>span.gs-name+span.gs-def div.glossary-columns>div.gc-line>span.gc-term+span.gc-def div.sources-list>a div.spoiler (see spoiler_minigame) - title slide only: div.title-slide>div.title-badge>img + div.kicker-line + h1 + p.lede + div.callout (keep an 'ask an AI when stuck' callout on the title slide).
content_language_convention: Prose and all UI-facing text: Greek. Code comments inside <pre><code>: English. Interface chrome (buttons, badges, system messages generated by script.js itself, e.g. 'Check', 'CORRECT!', 'Reset this quiz', 'Score: N%') is English by explicit choice, except the #final-score text which is intentionally Greek/English-mixed as specified above.
quiz_writing_rules: 4 options, similar length/style - no option stands out by size/detail
correct-answer position varies across questions, not always the same slot
distractors are plausible/related misconceptions, never eliminable by 'obviously silly' reasoning
include at least one distractor per deck that's deliberately ~5 words longer than the correct answer (tests the 'longer = more thorough = right' bias)
one short explanation shown after the answer is revealed
hard_constraints: never solve the actual student exercise/assignment in generated content - theory and tools only, leave design questions open
confirm a planned section list with the user before generating full lesson content, unless already confirmed
no gradients anywhere, no hardcoded colors outside the --tone-*/--syn-* token system

do not restructure static/script.js or static/style.css for a normal new-lesson request - only index.html content changes; engine changes are rare, deliberate, and go through all real files (index.html template + at least one real lesson file) to verify nothing breaks
current_deliverables: index.html (template, fully documented top comment, demo/placeholder content for every slide type)
lessons/07-Docker.html (cypress theme, real content), lessons/08-goroutines-channels.html (burgundy theme, real content)
lesson-generator-instructions.json, section-generator-instructions.json, section-generator-standalone.json - self-contained prompts for generating full lessons or single sections via any LLM
open_items_not_yet_done: spoiler reveal state is not persisted to localStorage (resets on reload) - flagged as acceptable for now

the user maintains their own working copies of index.html/style.css/script.js that may have diverged further since this brief was written - always ask for their current files before making further engine changes rather than assuming this brief's file contents are still exact
